tts: When we make a comparative sentence, we say than with a weak sound.
The nights are colder than the days.

items.x: The nights are colder than the days.
It isn’t as cold as yesterday.

sub.en: Look at the comparisons. When do you add -er, and when do you use more?

items.q: Today is ___ than yesterday.
items.why: Short adjectives take -er. Long ones (three syllables and most two-syllable ones) take more.

items.q: Tokyo is ___ than Singapore.
The summer here is ___ than it was.
items.why: consonant + y → -ier: dry → drier, happy → happier.

items.q: August is ___ than July.
items.why: One short vowel + one consonant → double the consonant: hot → hotter.

items.q: The weather is ___ than last year.
items.why: good → better, bad → worse. These two are irregular.

items.q: The pollution is ___ than it was.
Today isn’t ___ cold ___ yesterday.
items.why: as … as says the two things are the same. With not, it says the first is less.

items.q: Winter here is as wet ___ spring.

acts.title: The same city, thirty years apart
text: THEN. In 1994 the first snow in this city fell in the middle of October, and the river was frozen from December to March. Children walked to school on the ice. The summers were short and rarely hotter than twenty-eight degrees. People complained that it was too cold.

NOW. The first snow now falls in late November, and the river freezes for six weeks, not four months. Last July the temperature reached forty-one degrees — hotter than any July in the old records. The winters are milder and shorter than they were, but the summers are worse. People complain that it is too hot.
The forecast is easier to read than the climate: nobody knows what October will do next year.

use: Which is drier, A or B?
tts: Which city is drier, Dublin or Paris? — It’s close: both cities have a lot of rain, but Dublin’s wetter.

Which is bigger, the population of Sydney or Cairo? — Well, Cairo’s population is bigger than Sydney’s. Cairo has a population of over nine million, but Sydney’s is smaller, at just over four and a half million.

write.q: Compare the weather in your town now and thirty years ago, and compare your town with one other place: 6 sentences. Use at least four comparatives and one “as … as”.
write.model: The winters here are shorter and milder than they were thirty years ago. The first snow is later — in November, not October. The summers are much hotter: last July was hotter than any July my parents remember. Almaty is warmer than my town, but it isn’t as dry. The air is worse than it was, because there are more cars. The forecast is easier to read than the climate.

speak.q: Answer out loud: Is winter colder here than in the south? Which is wetter, spring or autumn? Is the weather better or worse than ten years ago?
speak.model: Yes, winter here is much colder than in the south. Autumn is wetter than spring. The winters are better than they were — milder — but the summers are worse.
